This {14} is made up of five themed splash pads—play areas where water sprays up from the ground—and a riverboat ride. There, guests in wheelchairs can {15} special waterproof chairs and enjoy the water without risking damage to their own wheelchairs. “Morgan taught me that there’s more to life in many ways than what I saw before,” said Hartman.

passage.title: 巴西戰舞卡波耶拉（Capoeira）
passage.text: Capoeira is a martial art—a style of fighting—that also includes acrobatics, drumming, singing, and dance. {11} its dancelike appearance, it shares many basic techniques with other martial arts. Capoeira was created nearly 500 years ago in Brazil by African slaves. {12} from their homes against their will, they first developed it as a means of self-defense. But before long, Capoeira was no longer only for protection; it also became a powerful weapon in their life-or-death struggle against the slave owners. When the owners realized the power of Capoeira, they began to punish anyone who practiced it. The slaves therefore learned to {13} the forbidden fights with singing, clapping, and dancing, as though Capoeira were simply entertainment. The slave owners were not the only ones against Capoeira. At first, the Brazilian government also {14} it. However, a man known as Mestre Bimba devoted a great deal of time and effort to convincing the government that it had great cultural value and should become an official fighting style. He succeeded and turned the martial art into Brazil’s national sport. Bimba was also among the first to open Capoeira schools, which helped the art {15} around the world. Nowadays, Capoeira can be seen in movies and music videos, and it is believed to have influenced breaking and other hip-hop dance styles.
